lesson.scenario: A bounded stream-stream join uses per-input watermarks to know when no future on-time match can arrive.
entities: Monotonic left, right, and operator frontiers

steps.title: Advance each input independently
steps.narration: Payments has observed max event time 10:08:30 with 30-second disorder, while Orders publishes only 10:06:40.

buffer.detail: No work accepted in this phase

timers.detail: No work accepted in this phase

output.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: The join records distinct monotonic completeness claims.
steps.invariant: Each input watermark and the operator minimum are monotonic; join state is retained until the minimum frontier passes the event maximum match horizon, and records older than that frontier use an explicit late-data path.

steps.title: Buffer a one-sided event
steps.narration: The join keeps P81 under O77 and registers cleanup at event time plus the two-minute match horizon, 10:09:20.
steps.outcome: The event remains eligible for a later order match.
steps.invariant: Each input watermark and the operator minimum are monotonic; join state is retained until the minimum frontier passes the event maximum match horizon, and records older than that frontier use an explicit late-data path.

steps.title: Hold to the slower frontier
steps.narration: Even though the payment side has passed 10:08, Orders at 10:06:40 may still provide O77 within the join interval, so the timer stays blocked.
steps.outcome: A slow active input prevents premature finalization.
steps.invariant: Each input watermark and the operator minimum are monotonic; join state is retained until the minimum frontier passes the event maximum match horizon, and records older than that frontier use an explicit late-data path.

steps.title: Join an on-time counterpart
steps.narration: The order lies 15 seconds before the payment and within the two-minute predicate; the state emits one pair identified by P81,O77 and marks it matched.
steps.outcome: The correlation is produced exactly once under checkpointed IDs.
steps.invariant: Each input watermark and the operator minimum are monotonic; join state is retained until the minimum frontier passes the event maximum match horizon, and records older than that frontier use an explicit late-data path.

steps.title: Finalize after both horizons pass
steps.narration: Only after both input watermarks exceed 10:09:20 does cleanup remove O77 state; a later O77 duplicate is classified late and cannot create a second base match.

output.detail: match revision=1; later duplicate -> late stream

production.scenario: TikTok ad impression billing waits for event-time completeness before charging advertisers for mobile and offline conversions.
components: global mobile apps and browsers sending impression and conversion events with clock skew and delay
service boundary that validates advertiser identity and normalizes raw event envelopes
control-plane service that estimates event-time completeness for billing windows across many shards
durable authority in Kafka and Delta Lake for raw events plus finalized billing facts
creates advertiser invoices and pacing signals from windows judged sufficiently complete
repair path that corrects invoices and pacing data when late events reopen a closed window
observability path for watermark skew, invoice corrections, and late-data exposure
flows: Ad clients upload impression and conversion events from devices with variable connectivity.
Normalized events are handed to the watermark service to estimate event-time completeness.
Only windows behind the completeness frontier are committed as stable billing facts.
Billing systems charge advertisers and feed pacing logic from durable sealed windows.
Late events that cross a closed boundary are routed into targeted billing correction workflows.
The repair worker reprocesses delayed events through the same watermark path to produce adjustments.
Dashboards track late-data volume, reopened invoice windows, and completeness confidence by region.
